questions.stem: Sucrose gives a negative result with Benedict's reagent. Why is this?

options.text: Sucrose is too large to dissolve in Benedict's reagent
Sucrose contains no carbon atoms so it cannot reduce copper ions
Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar because its glycosidic bond locks the reactive groups of glucose and fructose
Sucrose is a polysaccharide and only monosaccharides react with Benedict's reagent

questions.explanation: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar. The glycosidic bond between glucose and fructose involves both of their reactive (anomeric) groups, so neither can donate electrons to reduce the copper ions in Benedict's reagent.
